title: Shopping Cart Functions
story: You're building the backend for your friend's online bakery. Customers add croissants and cakes to their cart, discounts apply, and prices need formatting. Functions will make this a piece of cake.
why: Real-world business logic — price calculation, discounts, and formatting — maps naturally to small, composable functions.
analogy: A shopping cart is like a conveyor belt at a grocery checkout. Item A goes through the scanner (item_total), all items reach the discount station (apply_discount), and the receipt printer formats the final number (format_price). Each station does one job.
try_it: Add a `calculate_tax(total: Float64, tax_rate: Float64) -> Float64` function and insert it between the discount and format steps. Test with an 8% tax rate.
tips: Use Float64 for prices — money has decimals
Keep the pipeline order clear: totals -> discount -> format
apply_discount uses the formula `total * (1 - pct/100)` in expanded form
Each function is independently testable: you can verify item_total(10.0, 3) returns 30.0
common_mistakes: Using Int for prices — you'll lose cents
Forgetting to divide the percentage by 100.0 in apply_discount
Applying the discount BEFORE calculating item totals — order matters
